text: When I start a container from an image, how does it end up seeing all the image's layers as one filesystem?
answer: The layers are stacked in a union filesystem, and the container's root directory is set to that unified directory using chroot.

gold.quote: When the container starts, its root directory is set to the location of this unified directory, using `chroot`.

text: If I delete or edit files inside a running container, does that change the image it was started from?
answer: No, the container gets its own directory for changes, so the original image layers stay untouched.

gold.quote: This allows the container to make filesystem changes while allowing the original image layers to remain untouched.

text: My Intune deployment of Docker Desktop on Windows reports exit code 3010. Did the install fail?
answer: No, code 3010 means the installation succeeded but a reboot is required.

gold.quote: Return code 3010 means the installation succeeded but a reboot is required.

text: I'm adding Docker Desktop for Mac to Intune as a line-of-business app. Which file do I upload?
answer: Upload the Docker.pkg file.

gold.quote: Upload the `Docker.pkg` file and fill in the required details.

text: If I archive one of my old Docker Hub repos, will people who depend on it still be able to docker pull its images?
answer: Yes, users can still pull the images from an archived repository.

gold.quote: Users can still pull the images.

text: I'm in the Settings tab of my Docker Hub repo and clicked the archive option. What do I have to enter to confirm before it archives?
answer: You enter the name of your repository to confirm.

gold.quote: Enter the name of your repository to confirm.

text: I have a service in my compose file that I never gave a profile to. Will it start when I just run docker compose up?
answer: Yes, services without a profiles attribute are always enabled, so they start with a plain docker compose up.

gold.quote: Services without a `profiles` attribute are always enabled.

text: How do I turn on every profile in my compose file at once instead of listing them one by one?
answer: Run docker compose --profile "*" to enable all profiles at the same time.

gold.quote: If you want to enable all profiles at the same time, you can run `docker compose --profile "*"`.

text: I edited one RUN line in the middle of my Dockerfile. Will the steps after it still come from cache on the next build?
answer: No, once a layer is invalidated, all the layers after it are invalidated too, so they get rebuilt.

gold.quote: Once one layer is invalidated, all following layers are also invalidated.

text: My Node app reinstalls all its yarn packages on every build even when I only change source files. How should I order my Dockerfile to avoid that?
answer: Copy only package.json (and the lockfile) first, run the dependency install, and then copy the rest of the code.

gold.quote: So, start by copying only that file first, then install the dependencies, and finally copy everything else.

text: I'm setting up sign-in enforcement on Ubuntu laptops. Where do I need to put the registry.json file?
answer: On Linux, create it at /usr/share/docker-desktop/registry/registry.json.

gold.quote: Linux | `/usr/share/docker-desktop/registry/registry.json

text: In our Mac MDM profile I want some internal hosts to skip the proxy. Which key do I use and how do I list multiple hosts?
answer: Use overrideProxyExclude with a comma-separated list of hosts and domains.

gold.quote: - `overrideProxyExclude`: Bypasses proxy settings for the specified hosts and domains. Uses a comma-separated list.

text: I want docker scout watch to keep re-checking my registry for new repositories while it runs. Which flag does that?
answer: Use the `--refresh-registry` flag, which periodically refreshes the repository lists.

gold.quote: - Periodically refresh repository lists, using `--refresh-registry

text: I'm connecting Scout to Artifactory and the --registry string has a `port` key. What is it used for, and is it required?
answer: It's the local port that docker scout watch listens on for webhook callbacks, and it's optional.

gold.quote: port`           |    No    | Local port to listen on for webhook callbacks.

text: I manage our company's Docker Hub org and want to stop people from making new public repos. Which roles can turn that on, and can I do the same for my personal account?
answer: Organization owners and editors can disable public repository creation for an organization namespace, but it can't be configured for personal account namespaces.

gold.quote:
Organization owners and editors can prevent creating public repositories within
organization namespaces.

text: My autobuilds email me every time a build finishes, which is too noisy. Which notification setting should I pick to get emails only when a build breaks?
answer: Choose the "Only failures" option under Settings > Notifications.

gold.quote: - **Only failures**: Only notifications about failed builds.

text: I have a Dockerfile with a few stages and I just run docker build without any extra flags. Which stage ends up being built?
answer: Docker builds the last stage in the Dockerfile by default unless you pick another stage with --target.

gold.quote: This means that if you don't explicitly specify a target stage using the `--target` flag in the `docker build` command, Docker will automatically build the last stage by default.

text: My single-stage Spring Boot image is 880MB. How big should it get if I split the Dockerfile into a JDK build stage and a JRE runtime stage?
answer: About 428 MB, down from 880 MB.

gold.quote: Your final image is just 428 MB, compared to the original build size of 880 MB.

text: Docker Scout flagged a high severity CVE-2022-24999 in my Node app because of an old express version. Which express version should I upgrade to in order to get rid of it?
answer: Upgrade express to version 4.17.3, which fixes the vulnerability.

gold.quote: The version 4.17.3 of the express package fixes the vulnerability.

text: I ran docker scout quickview and some of my policies show a question mark instead of a check or an exclamation mark. What does that mean?
answer: A question mark means there isn't enough metadata to complete the policy evaluation.

gold.quote: Question marks indicate that there isn't enough metadata to complete the evaluation.

text: A new Docker Desktop version came out and I'm on RHEL. Can I just install the new RPM over my current one?
answer: No, you need to remove the previous version first and then install the newly downloaded package.

gold.quote: You need to first remove the previous version and then download the new package each time you want to upgrade Docker Desktop.

text: I run KDE instead of GNOME on my RHEL box and Docker Desktop can't open a terminal. What do I need to install?
answer: Install gnome-terminal.

gold.quote: If you're not using GNOME, you must install `gnome-terminal` to enable terminal access from Docker Desktop:

text: My docker scout cves output is full of CVEs that my team has already marked as not applicable. How do I hide those from the results?
answer: Run docker scout cves with the --ignore-suppressed flag.

gold.quote: To exclude suppressed CVEs from the output, use the `--ignore-suppressed` flag:

text: I created exceptions in Docker Scout, but the CLI doesn't show them. What command do I run to point the CLI at my organization?
answer: Run docker scout configure organization <organization>, using the same organization you created the exceptions in.

gold.quote: > $ docker scout configure organization <organization>

text: I switched to the new VMM on my M-series Mac and now my amd64 images run really slowly. Why is that?
answer: Docker VMM doesn't currently support Rosetta, so amd64 emulation is slow.

gold.quote: Docker VMM does not currently support Rosetta, so emulation of amd64 architectures is slow.

text: I installed Docker Desktop on Windows just for my own user and don't have admin rights. Can I run the Linux VM with Hyper-V?
answer: No, Hyper-V is only available in all-users installation mode and requires administrator privileges.

gold.quote: Hyper-V is only available in all-users installation mode and requires administrator privileges.

text: When I'm looking at the usage chart for my org's images, what time ranges can I pick from?
answer: You can select a time interval of 3, 6, or 12 months.

gold.quote: - Select the time interval: 3, 6, or 12 months

text: I downloaded the summary CSV for my publisher org and there's an EVENT_COUNT column. How is that number calculated?
answer: It is the sum of data downloads and version checks.

gold.quote: EVENT_COUNT`      | The total number of events, calculated as the sum of data downloads and version checks.

text: I'm moving my private images over to a second personal Docker account. I've pulled them while signed in to my old account. What do I do to them before pushing so they land in the new account?
answer: Tag each image with your new Docker username as the namespace, then log in with the new account and push.

gold.quote: Tag your private images with your newly created Docker username, for example:

text: I want to copy my private images from my own account into a company org on Docker Hub. What should I confirm about my membership before I start pulling and pushing?
answer: Confirm that your user account is a member of the organization you're moving the images to.

gold.quote: Select the applicable organization and verify that your user account is a member of the organization.

text: I ran docker scout cves on an image I don't have on my machine yet. Will it fail, or what happens?
answer: Docker pulls the image first and then runs the analysis.

gold.quote: If the image doesn't exist locally, Docker pulls the image before running the analysis.

text: I saved an image to a .tar file with docker save and want Scout to analyze that file directly. Which prefix do I put in front of it?
answer: Use the `archive://` prefix.

gold.quote: archive://`         | Use a tarball archive, as created by `docker save

text: I recreated my containers after changing my compose config. Will they keep the same IP address, and can I hardcode the IP to connect them?
answer: No, IPs are assigned dynamically and change on restart or recreation, so you should always reference services by name instead.

gold.quote: Docker assigns container IP addresses dynamically from the network's subnet each time a container starts so they are not persisted across restarts or recreations.

text: One of my services should have no network access at all. How do I turn off networking for just that container in Compose?
answer: Set `network_mode: none` on that service.

gold.quote: none`: Turns off all container networking.

text: I want to run a Docker Scout CVE scan in my CircleCI pipeline. Which file in my repo do I put the config in?
answer: Put it in a .circleci/config.yml file.

gold.quote: Add the following to a _.circleci/config.yml_ file.

text: In the CircleCI Scout example, which Docker version does the remote Docker environment use for running docker commands?
answer: Version 20.10.24.

gold.quote: version: 20.10.24

text: If I delete one of my containers, will that break the other containers I have running?
answer: No, each container is managed independently, so deleting one doesn't affect the others.

gold.quote: Independent. Each container is independently managed. Deleting one container won't affect any others.

text: I stopped a container and now it doesn't show up when I run docker ps. How do I see it in the list?
answer: Add the -a flag, i.e. run `docker ps -a`, to list stopped containers as well.

gold.quote: To view stopped containers, add the `-a` flag to list all containers: `docker ps -a

text: I bought a subscription on my personal Docker account but now want to move it to my company's organization. Can I transfer it?
answer: No, subscriptions can't be transferred between accounts or organizations.

gold.quote: Subscriptions are non-transferable between accounts or organizations.

text: I'm based in Germany. Since when has Docker been adding VAT to its invoices?
answer: Docker began collecting VAT from European customers on March 1, 2025.

gold.quote: For European customers, Docker began collecting VAT on March 1, 2025.

text: How many different rulesets am I allowed to attach to a single OIDC connection?
answer: You can add between one and five rulesets on a connection.

gold.quote: You can add one to five rulesets on a connection.

text: What should I put as the subject claim if I only want the main branch of one specific repo in my org to be able to authenticate?
answer: Use `repo:my-org/my-repo:ref:refs/heads/main`, which matches only the main branch of that repository.

gold.quote:
Pattern                                        | Matches                                              |
| :--------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------- |
| `repo:my-org/my-repo:ref:refs/heads/main`      | Only the `main` branch of a specific repository

text: My Docker Hub autobuild keeps getting cancelled and I never clicked cancel. How long can a build run before it's killed automatically?
answer: Automated builds are automatically cancelled once they hit the 4-hour execution time limit.

gold.quote: Automated builds have a 4-hour execution time limit.

text: My repo pulls in private git submodules and the autobuild can't clone them. What do I name the build environment variable where I paste my private key?
answer: Name the environment variable SSH_PRIVATE and paste the private half of the keypair into its value.

gold.quote: Enter `SSH_PRIVATE` as the name for the new environment variable.

text: I set up my company's org on Docker Hub last week and picked the wrong namespace. Can I change it to something else?
answer: No, the organization namespace is permanent and can't be changed after the organization is created.

gold.quote:
You can't change it after you create the
  organization.

text: My personal Docker ID is already taken by a username I use. Can I create an organization that uses that same name as its namespace?
answer: No, Docker IDs and organization namespaces must be unique, so an organization can't use a namespace that matches an existing Docker ID.

gold.quote: Docker IDs and organization namespaces must be unique.

text: I'm using the Docker SDK in my Python script on Linux with Docker Desktop and it says it can't connect to the daemon at /var/run/docker.sock, even though the docker CLI works fine. Where is the socket actually located?
answer: Docker Desktop for Linux uses a per-user socket at ~/.docker/desktop/docker.sock instead of /var/run/docker.sock, so SDKs need DOCKER_HOST set to point to it.

gold.quote: Docker Desktop for Linux uses a per-user socket located at `~/.docker/desktop/docker.sock` instead of the system-wide `/var/run/docker.sock`.

text: I deleted a bunch of images but my Docker disk image file is called Docker.qcow2 and I don't see the space back on my drive yet. How long until it's freed?
answer: With Docker.qcow2, a background process frees the space after a few minutes.

gold.quote: If the file is named `Docker.qcow2`: space will be freed by a background process after a few minutes.

text: I'm on a work laptop where I don't have admin rights, so I'd do the per-user install of Docker Desktop. Can I run Windows containers with that?
answer: No, Windows containers are not supported with the per-user installation; they require the all-users installation.

gold.quote: Windows containers | Not supported | Supported

text: I'm installing Docker Desktop from the command line and want it in a different folder than the default. Which installer option do I use?
answer: Use the `--installation-dir=<path>` flag to change the default install location.

gold.quote: --installation-dir=<path>`: Changes the default installation location (`C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker`)

text: My company runs our Windows desktops on Nutanix VDI. Will Docker support Docker Desktop there?
answer: Yes, as long as the underlying Windows environment supports WSL 2 or Windows container mode.

gold.quote: Nutanix-powered VDI | Supported, provided the underlying Windows environment supports WSL 2 or Windows container mode.

text: Our virtual desktop gets wiped back to a fresh image every time someone logs off, so we reinstall Docker Desktop each session. Is that setup covered by Docker support?
answer: No, non-persistent VDI environments where the OS resets between sessions are not supported.

gold.quote: Non-persistent VDI environments: not supported. Docker Desktop doesn't support environments where the OS resets between sessions, requiring re-installation or reconfiguration each time.

text: I removed our domain from the SSO connection and now want to add it back. Do I need to redo the DNS verification?
answer: Yes, Docker assigns a new TXT record value when you re-add a domain, so you must complete domain verification again with it.

gold.quote: When you re-add a domain, Docker assigns a new TXT record value.

text: Which Docker provisioning option keeps the users and groups in our identity provider synced into Docker?
answer: SCIM provisioning.

gold.quote: - SCIM provisioning: Sync users and groups from your identity provider to Docker

text: I want to write my own converter image for Compose Bridge. Where does my container read the Compose file from, and where should it write the generated files?
answer: The image reads the resolved Compose model from /in/compose.yaml and writes any target format files under /out.

gold.quote: A transformation is packaged as a Docker image that receives the fully-resolved Compose model as `/in/compose.yaml` and can produce any target format file under `/out`.

text: When customizing a Compose Bridge template, which helper function can I use to encode a value for a Kubernetes secret?
answer: The `base64` function, which encodes a string as base64.

gold.quote: base64`    | Encodes a string as base64 (used for Kubernetes secrets).

text: I want to turn off JIT provisioning for my SSO connection. What do I need to have enabled before I can do that?
answer: You must have SCIM enabled, because at least one provisioning method has to stay on.

gold.quote: If you want to turn JIT off, then you must have SCIM enabled; conversely, if you want to turn SCIM off, you must re-enable JIT.

text: If someone leaves our company, will JIT provisioning remove their Docker account?
answer: No, JIT only creates users and applies attributes from the SSO assertion, and it doesn't deprovision users.

gold.quote: Just-in-Time (JIT)](/security/provisioning/just-in-time/) | When a user signs in through SSO | Creates users and applies attributes from the SSO assertion. It doesn't deprovision users | Enabled when you configure SSO

text: When I run a container from an image I don't have on my machine yet, where does Docker download it from?
answer: Docker pulls the image from your configured registry, which is Docker Hub by default.

gold.quote: When you use the `docker pull` or `docker run` commands, Docker pulls the required images from your configured registry.

text: If I install Docker Desktop, do I also get Compose and Kubernetes, or do I have to install those separately?
answer: Docker Desktop bundles Docker Compose and Kubernetes, along with the daemon, the client, Docker Content Trust and Credential Helper.

gold.quote: Docker Desktop includes the Docker daemon (`dockerd`), the Docker client (`docker`), Docker Compose, Docker Content Trust, Kubernetes, and Credential Helper.
